references.text: Thematic parallel showing the fathers' fear of losing their possessions/children, but with opposite direction in the conflict (sons against father vs. father against sons).
Direct narrative connection where 31:16 provides the theological answer to the accusations made in 31:1.
Links the accusation of theft (31:1) with Laban's counterargument regarding the family's and property's ownership (31:43).

Thematic contrast between the son's unjust claim to inheritance (Luke) and the accusation that Jacob has taken all the father's possessions (Genesis), both touching on the family's economic breakdown.
Narrative contrast showing the development in Laban's attitude toward Jacob: from a warm welcome (29:13) to hostile accusations through his sons (31:1).
Theological contrast between Jesus' unity with the Father where all is shared (John) and the human conflict where sons accuse their father of taking everything (Genesis).
